children: Indian corporate earnings delivered a stronger-than-expected performance in the July-September 2026 quarter, with 28 out of the sectors tracked by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) meeting or exceeding estimates, according to the brokerage’s quarterly review released in November 2026.

The MOFSL Universe of 398 companies reported sales, EBITDA, and PAT growth of 25 per cent, 23 per cent, and 32 per cent year-on-year respectively, surpassing estimates of 19 per cent, 17 per cent, and 21 per cent. Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings grew 30 per cent YoY. The Nifty-50 recorded 27 per cent YoY PAT growth — its highest in 17 quarters — led by Reliance Industries, ONGC, Tata Motors PV, JSW Steel, and SBI, which together accounted for 46 per cent of the incremental earnings accretion.

BFSI, Metals, Oil & Gas, and Automobiles were the primary drivers, collectively contributing 77 per cent to the incremental year-on-year earnings growth. The EBITDA margin for non-financial companies came in at 17.5 per cent, slightly ahead of the estimated 17.0 per cent, despite elevated input cost pressures during the quarter.

Across market capitalisation segments, large-caps posted 31 per cent PAT growth against an estimate of 24 per cent, while mid-caps grew 22 per cent and small-caps outperformed at 32 per cent YoY. The beat-to-miss ratio remained favourable, with 42 per cent of companies exceeding PAT estimates and 26 per cent missing them.

On the earnings revision front, the Nifty EPS estimate for FY27 was raised marginally by 0.9 per cent to INR 1,243, while the FY28 estimate was upgraded 1.4 per cent to INR 1,427. JSW Steel, BSE, and Reliance Industries led the upgrades.

Looking ahead, MOFSL expects MOFSL Universe and Nifty earnings growth of 11 per cent and 18 per cent respectively in the second half of FY27. Excluding OMCs, the MOFSL Universe is projected to report 20 per cent earnings growth in 2HFY27, with Metals, Private Banks, and NBFCs expected to remain key contributors.

title: India Inc posts broad-based earnings beat in Q2FY27; Nifty PAT hits 17-quarter high
